name: Position debate
how: Each debater owns one candidate answer and argues for it against the others.

name: Scientific disprove
how: Each debater owns one hypothesis, and the job is to disprove the others with evidence.
when: Root cause: why is this happening.

name: Steelman tournament
how: Before rebutting, each debater must restate the opponent's case better than the opponent did.

name: Blind first, one reveal
how: Everyone answers alone first, then sees the others once, then revises once. Report the spread, not just the consensus.
when: Default for anything with a checkable answer.

name: Method cards
how: Each debater uses a different reasoning method (first principles, analogy, base rates, working backwards), not a different persona.
when: Reasoning problems where everyone keeps making the same mistake.

name: Calibrated critic
how: One critic is strict but not absolute: it must find real flaws and may concede. A separate judge breaks ties.
source: DEBATE (arXiv 2405.09935): +6.4pp over G-Eval; MAD (2305.19118): modest disagreement beats total

name: Authentic dissent (red team)
how: Give one debater a genuinely conflicting goal (the competitor's, the customer's, the budget owner's) and the job of defeating the plan. The decider rules after both sides fight.
when: Strategy and plans where everyone already agrees.
source: Nemeth 2001 (authentic dissent beats an assigned devil's advocate); Huawei blue army (蓝军)

name: Opposite with equal rigour
how: After the case for, demand the case against with the same rigour and the same length.

name: PR-FAQ attack
how: Write the launch press release and the hardest customer and internal FAQ first. Reviewers attack only the FAQ answers.

name: Cross-model review
how: A different model family reviews the work. Every claim needs evidence, and no concession without a reason.
when: Code review and anything where one model's blind spot matters.
source: Milvus code-review test: 53% of bugs solo vs 80% with 5 models (15 PRs, directional)
